card.keepWhy: Something new is springing up now.
sources: Isaiah 43:16 (the Lord “who makes a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters”)
Isaiah 43:18 (“Don’t remember the former things, and don’t consider the things of old”; common modern rendering “do not dwell on the past”)
Isaiah 43:19 (“Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don’t you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert”)
Exodus 14 (the crossing of the sea), the “former things” the exiles remembered
2 Kings 25:8-11 (Jerusalem and the temple burned by the Babylonians; people carried into exile)
Ezra 1:1-4 (Cyrus of Persia lets the exiles return to rebuild, 538 BC)
Psalm 137:1-2 (by the rivers of Babylon; harps on the willows), behind painting PA1 only
check: Many scholars date Isaiah 40-55 to the exile (often called Second Isaiah); the lesson says “a prophet” in the captions and names Isaiah only in the source line. Confirm this is acceptable.
Captions blend the World English Bible with the common modern phrase “don’t dwell on the past” (as in the app’s class text). Confirm wording.
The lesson reads the “former things” (43:18) as including the sea crossing just recalled in 43:16-17, a common reading; some read them as the exile’s disasters or earlier prophecies. Confirm.

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? ever replayed an old mistake for the hundredth time? or missed the good old days so much it hurt?
options: then this one was written for you. it was first said to people who were homesick.
i’m glad you’re here. hold that while you listen.
good. keep this one for a friend who’s stuck.

steps.line: Long ago, the people of Israel lived far from home, in exile in Babylon. Jerusalem lay in ruins behind them.
They told the old stories again and again. One they loved most: how God led their ancestors out of Egypt, on a path straight through the sea.
Then a prophet brought God’s message. He spoke of the God “who makes a way in the sea, a path in the mighty waters.”
steps.label: Isaiah 43:16

steps.line: And then: “Don’t remember the former things, and don’t dwell on the past.”
steps.label: Isaiah 43:18

steps.q: The “former things” included the escape from Egypt, the greatest rescue in their story. Why tell them not to dwell on it?
o: Because the escape no longer mattered
So old glory wouldn’t blind them to now
Because it was a painful memory
steps.why: It wasn’t a bad memory. But even a holy memory can keep you stuck, looking backward while God begins something new.

steps.q: These chapters of Isaiah, spoken to the exiles, open with which words?
o: “Hear, O Israel, the Lord is one”
steps.why: Isaiah 40 opens with comfort, said twice. Earlier chapters warned; these console people who had lost everything. Handel set the line to music in Messiah.

steps.q: God promises a new thing, out in the dry wilderness. What do you guess he says he’ll make there?
steps.why: A road and rivers. In a desert, that means a way home, and life where nothing grows.

steps.line: “Look, I am doing a new thing. It springs up now. Don’t you see it? I will make a road in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.”
steps.label: Isaiah 43:19

steps.q: Did the exiles ever get home?
o: Yes: a Persian king let them go
Yes, after a war of rebellion
No: they stayed in Babylon for good
steps.why: In 539 BCE Cyrus of Persia took Babylon and let exiled peoples go home. The prophet even calls him God’s “anointed”: a foreign king doing God’s work.

steps.line: Years later, the exiles were allowed to go home. They walked back across the wilderness and began to rebuild Jerusalem.
steps.label: Ezra 1

say: here’s what i love. this promise wasn’t for people whose life was going well. it was for people who thought their best days were over.
jews and christians have both held onto it: God’s best work isn’t only behind you. it’s springing up now, if you look.

steps.q: The prophet says “don’t dwell on the past,” yet he opens by remembering the path through the sea. What does that suggest?
o: The new rescue will copy the old one
The old stories should now be set aside
Remember the past, but expect something new
steps.why: He doesn’t erase the old story. He uses it as a reason to expect a new one: the God who made a path then is making a road now.

today.say: when an old mistake, or the good old days, starts replaying today, say to yourself, “that was then.” then look for one new thing springing up now, and name it. if you like, make it a one-line thank-you prayer: watch, learn, or join in. your choice.
options: good. that’s the prophet’s whole message. look, it springs up now.
then you know exactly where to start. that was then. what’s new?
